title: Inauguration of the U.P. Film Center.
description: Formal inauguration of the U.P. Film Center Fine Arts Complex, featuring speeches of Imelda Marcos, awards, and recognition of leading Filipino filmmakers.
full_description: The formal inauguration of the U.P. Film Center Fine Arts Complex marked the opening of the University of the Philippines Film Center’s dedicated facilities and its establishment as a major institutional venue for film education, exhibition, production, research, and cultural activities. Imelda Romualdez-Marcos was invited to the inaugural event, while writer and filmmaker Virginia R. Moreno delivered a speech. Three young Filipino filmmakers—Lino Brocka, Ishmael Bernal, and Eddie Romero—were presented with awards during the ceremony. In lieu of the customary cornerstone, an antique jar containing a film reel and a painter’s palette was buried as the inauguration’s ceremonial foundation object. The ritual symbolized cinema’s relationship with earlier artistic traditions and expressed the idea that modern cinema could serve both as a user and preserver of older arts and of life itself. Following its inauguration, the Film Center operated as a central workshop for cinematic studies, developed the beginnings of a film research archive, and served as a showcase theater for Filipino and international cinema. The event consequently marked an important moment in the institutional establishment of film as an academic, artistic, archival, and cultural practice at the University of the Philippines.

title: Gala Premiere of The Story of Adele H., 80 Years of French Cinema.
description: Gala benefit premiere of The Story of Adele H. celebrating 80 years of French cinema and supporting young filmmakers.
full_description:
The U.P. Film Center, in collaboration with the French Embassy, the Writers’ Union of the Philippines, and the Manila Film Society, presented a gala benefit premiere of François Truffaut’s The Story of Adele H., starring Isabelle Adjani, at the Rizal Theater on September 7, 1976. The event formed part of the celebration of 80 Years of French Cinema and was organized in support of the Young Filmmakers’ Fellowship Fund to France.

The gala brought together representatives of the Philippine and French cultural communities, filmmakers, writers, artists, patrons, and other supporters of cinema. It highlighted the U.P. Film Center’s role in presenting significant international films to Philippine audiences while fostering cultural exchange and connections between Filipino and French cinema.

The program included institutional and diplomatic messages, including those of Imelda Romualdez Marcos and Guy de Lestrange, Ambassadeur de France aux Philippines, as well as commentaries on the film and filmmaking by Filipino writers, poets, filmmakers, and film practitioners. Among those represented were Virginia R. Moreno, Adrian Cristobal, Jorge Arago, Ishmael Bernal, Romeo Vitug, Beatriz Romualdez-Francia, and U.P. Film Center archivist Annela Mendoza.

The event also acknowledged its patrons and institutional supporters, including Banque Nationale de Paris and Services Franco-Belges. Beyond its presentation of Truffaut’s film, the gala demonstrated the U.P. Film Center’s broader cultural and educational mission: to promote film appreciation, facilitate international cultural exchange, and support the development of Filipino filmmakers through opportunities for training and fellowship abroad.

title: New German Cinema [Das neue kino] Program: Three Aprils Celebration.
description: A U.P. Film Center and Goethe House program showcasing New German Cinema as part of a three-Aprils celebration.
full_description:
The U.P. Film Center and the Goethe House German Cultural Center presented The New German Cinema, a film program held from April 24 to May 1, 1977, at the Metropolitan Museum, Central Bank Complex, Roxas Boulevard. The program formed part of a broader “Three Aprils of a Life in Films” celebration organized by the U.P. Film Center and the President’s Council on the Arts of the University of the Philippines.

The program featured a selection of films associated with the New German Cinema movement, introducing Philippine audiences to significant developments in contemporary German filmmaking. Screenings were accompanied by film notes, synopses, critical views, and reviews intended to provide audiences with historical and cultural context for the films and their filmmakers.

The event also highlighted the cultural and educational partnership between the U.P. Film Center and the Goethe House German Cultural Center. Through the presentation of German films and related critical materials, the program contributed to the Film Center’s broader mission of film education, international cultural exchange, and the promotion of cinema as an artistic and intellectual practice.

The celebration included messages from Dr. Gerrit Bretzler, Director of the Goethe House, German Cultural Center, and Virginia R. Moreno, Director of the U.P. Film Center. It also presented the Film Center’s accomplishments and activities through its “Dream Rationale and Night Powers of the Film Center” section. The program concluded with acknowledgements to participating institutions and supporters and announced an upcoming French Film Festival, further reflecting the Film Center’s sustained engagement with international cinema.

title: Swedish Film Festival.
description: A festival of Swedish cinema presented by the U.P. Film Center, Swedish Embassy, and Manila Film Society
full_description:
The U.P. Film Center, in collaboration with the Swedish Embassy and the Manila Film Society, presented the Swedish Film Festival from December 2 to 7, 1977, at the Philippine International Convention Center. The festival formed part of the Film Center’s program of international cinema and cultural exchange, bringing Swedish films to Philippine audiences.

The festival opened with a program featuring selected works of Swedish cinema and included materials introducing audiences to the films and their directors. The program also featured a lecture forum by visiting Swedish film director Vilgot Sjöman and screenings of notable Swedish films, including Ingmar Bergman’s Cries and Whispers, Sjöman’s A Handful of Love, and Bo Widerberg’s Elvira Madigan. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

The event reflected the U.P. Film Center’s continuing efforts to expand Philippine audiences’ access to international cinema while developing cultural and institutional partnerships with foreign diplomatic and film organizations. The festival was supported by the Royal Swedish Embassy and the Manila Film Society, with Kjell Anneling, Charge d’Affaires a.i. of the Royal Swedish Embassy, and Virginia R. Moreno, Director of the U.P. Film Center, contributing messages to the program.

The festival program also highlighted the Film Center’s activities and accomplishments and included a poem by Virginia R. Moreno, a schedule of screenings, notes on the films and directors, and information about the Manila Film Society, including its Board of Directors, patrons, and donors.
